object_description: simple two-storey building with a differentiated folded roof landscape closing the break area
geometry_property: longitudinal facade closing the break area
mixed concrete rib and column system
design_condition: the replacement building follows the orientation of the existing school and closes the spacious break area to the west with its longitudinal facade, clearly subordinated to the listed main building

positive: The building follows the orientation of the existing school and closes the break area to the west
The simple two-storey building is clearly subordinated to the listed main building
The differentiated roof shape gives it identity and an independent presence
The covered open outside space at the front improves and relieves the access situation
The public pedestrian connection between the two buildings is retained
The opportunity of the two-storey structure is well used by the differentiated roof landscape
The two-storey auditorium and classrooms benefit from better daylight yield
They also gain optimal natural ventilation options
Two staircases are reached via two foyers, each with a fountain
The ground floor contains all semi-public rooms used by the whole school
The upper floor contains all more private uses
The central wide corridor zone offers diverse usable zones for working and playing
The view down into the auditorium can additionally light this communal area
The plan corresponds to the guiding principle of becoming a living space in a big way
Adding the corridor zone rather than the library as auditorium extension makes everyday sense
The library keeps its independence and character
The interior surfaces of classrooms, group rooms and corridor zones are mostly proposed in wood
With few load-bearing walls upstairs a variety of alternative spatial plans is possible
Even with changed divisions the spaces never appear banal, characterless or anonymous
They always retain a very high level of identity thanks to the three-dimensional room design
negative: The large footprint shrinks the outside areas in the west and south to residual areas
The covered connection with a suspended textile roof is neither operationally nor architecturally convincing
The public pedestrian connection remains somewhat undefined
The complex statics carry structural and financial risks difficult to predict at this stage
The less compact flat structure has a cost-increasing effect
The building has average figures in floor space and building volume
